narrationScript: For our final hands-on challenge, you'll apply what you've learned about dynamic memory allocation. Your task is to write a C program that calculates the average of user-entered grades. First, you'll prompt the user for the number of grades they want to enter. Based on this input, you'll dynamically allocate an array of floats on the heap to store these grades. Remember to use `malloc` and crucially, check if the allocation was successful by comparing the returned pointer to `NULL`. Then, use a loop to prompt the user to enter each grade and store it in your dynamically allocated array. After collecting all grades, calculate and print their average. And most importantly, before your program exits, ensure you free the dynamically allocated memory using `free` and set your pointer to `NULL`. This practice is vital for preventing memory leaks and ensuring responsible resource management. Take your time, refer to the examples, and build this program step-by-step. Good luck!
deliveryNotes: Stress the importance of `free` and nullifying the pointer.
